The website as a "showcase" is a metaphor i.e. starting to age.

When choices are made not only by a person but also by their AI agent, a beautiful facade loses weight. What matters more to the agent is not the tone of the page, but what can be structurally read and verified.

So the question changes.
Not "how to look convincing", but "what in the business is verifiable".

In the article, I examine the idea of a website as a verifiable representation: a single source of truth, machine-readable facts, signed claims where accountability exists, and a human at the point of final confirmation.

Without hype. Simply as an architectural shift that makes sense to start preparing for now.
